claims.text: The initial equiatomic FeCoNi alloy is a single-phase FCC material.
Equiatomic FCC FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Equiatomic FCC FeCoNi has low coercivity and is a soft ferromagnet.
Previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives exhibit low-coercivity soft ferromagnetism.
Adding Mn in an equiatomic proportion produces FeCoNiMn with approximately 25 at.% of each element.
Equiatomic FeCoNiMn has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Suitable melting and homogenization can produce a uniform, single-phase FCC FeCoNiMn alloy without significant clustering or secondary phases.
Mn addition enhances local lattice distortion in FeCoNiMn.
Mn addition introduces nanoscale regions with antiferromagnetic tendencies in FeCoNiMn.
Mn introduces localized antiferromagnetic exchange couplings and associated lattice strain.
The Mn-induced distortions and antiferromagnetic regions act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Mn-induced local distortions increase magnetic anisotropy.
The proposed pinning and anisotropy increase the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
Equiatomic FeCoNiMn will have higher coercivity than equiatomic FeCoNi.
Equiatomic FeCoNiMn will have higher coercivity than the previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
The coercivity enhancement will occur without appreciably reducing saturation magnetization.
The proposed coercivity enhancement applies only while FeCoNiMn remains an equiatomic, single-phase high-entropy solid solution.
Phase separation, ordering, or secondary-compound formation may negate the coercivity enhancement.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires FeCoNiMn to outperform FeCoNi and the Pd/Pt derivatives, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only when both comparisons fail. Thus, failure to outperform one required comparator can leave the hypothesis unrejected.
